cfb_lead44_sandwich_fade_on_benchmark.description: LEAD-44 CFB sandwich/lookahead fade: AP-ranked host (proxy: trailing market-line rating in the top quintile of that season-week's field) vs unranked visitor (below that quintile), where the host's own next scheduled game is a rivalry pair (8-consecutive-season proxy) or against a top-8th-percentile-rated opponent. Rule B (fade the host in that sandwich spot) minus Rule A (always back the ranked host), scored on the XLG-03 clean-core benchmark population.
cfb_lead44_sandwich_fade_on_benchmark.notes: AP poll table absent from data/cfb and data/raw (measured, docs/cfb_lead_screens_wave1.md section 4 confirms this was still true as of 2026-09-05; re-measured this session, still true) -- ranked/unranked status is a LABELLED PROXY from trailing market-line strength, not a real poll; disclosed throughout docs/lookahead_fade.md. Eligible population (ranked host x unranked visitor, both ratings defined) = 1622 games; scored (clean-core seasons only) = 1185; flagged (marquee-next) = 681; matched control = 504. Raw home-cover rate: flagged 49.03% [45.55,52.42] vs control 52.81% [48.10,57.38] -- same direction as the Rule-B delta (ranked hosts cover LESS in sandwich spots), not independently bootstrapped as a joint gap (each group's own week-blocked CI reported instead). Reliability: this is a per-game situational construct (this week's schedule position), not a persistent per-team trait -- same category as the existing registry entry bias_battery_sandwich_spot_opener ('not_applicable ... per-game situational condition ... nothing to split-half', read from registry/weak_signals.json), so --reliability is left unset here. Closest analogous check, an odd/even-season split of the same Rule-B-minus-A delta: odd seasons -0.485pts [-6.616,+5.355] P+ 0.455; even seasons +2.909pts [-2.072,+7.891] P+ 0.875 -- both cross zero, directionally noisy, not a resolved disagreement. CFB is close-graded (no verified CFB opener); settles no NFL play/no-play decision by itself. Spends no rotation window (CFB is free ground per docs/rotation_registry.md rule 8) and pools with no other CFB family.
cfb_lead44_sandwich_fade_on_benchmark.plain_summary: When a strong team hosts a weak team right before a rivalry game or a matchup with another strong team, that favorite covers a bit less often than usual (a lean, not yet proven).
